summary: A tremolo for the SDK tutorial: a low-frequency oscillator moves the level, with a sine or triangle shape, a phase offset between the channels and Mix and Amount. Use it for swells, pulses and a slow stereo pan.
use_for: Swells, pulses and slow stereo pans: moves the level up and down in time.

parameters.name: Rate
parameters.how: Sets how many times a second the level moves down and up, from 0.1 to 20 Hz.
parameters.sound: Slow rates swell like breathing; fast rates flutter and become a buzz.

parameters.name: Depth
parameters.description: How far the level moves down
parameters.how: Sets how far the level falls at the bottom of each cycle: 0 % none, 100 % to silence.
parameters.sound: More depth makes the pulse deeper and more obvious.

parameters.name: Shape
parameters.how: Chooses the shape of the movement: Sine or Triangle.
parameters.sound: Sine is smooth and round; Triangle is sharper and more mechanical.

parameters.name: Phase
parameters.description: Phase offset of the right channel
parameters.how: Delays the right channel's movement against the left, from 0 to 180 degrees.
parameters.sound: At 180 degrees one side is loud while the other is quiet, so the sound pans from side to side.

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Dry/wet (the effect has no latency, so the dry signal is not delayed)
parameters.how: Blends the tremolo with the unprocessed sound.
parameters.sound: Lower values keep the original level steady and add the pulse as a layer.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: Effect strength: 100 % = the settings as shown, 0 % = bypass (bit for bit the input), 200 % = twice as far from neutral
parameters.how: Scales Depth. 0 % is bypass, 100 % your settings, 200 % twice as far from neutral.
parameters.sound: Turn it down to ease the tremolo in, up to push it harder.
